Behind the work

Hi! I'm a Biomedical and Mechanical Engineering student at McMaster University. Whether it's a wearable sensor tracking a child's gait or a linkage modeled to one patient's specific anatomy, I like starting from the clinical problem and designing backward into the mechanism.

I'm especially passionate about medical device development and rehabilitation technology, anywhere engineering can hand someone back a little more independence, and I'm always excited to find the next place biomedical engineering can actually help.

02 — Where I've worked

Work Experience

  • Designed and prototyped a wrist-worn IMU wearable in SolidWorks with a pediatric-optimized housing and strap for objective movement disorder monitoring.
  • Contributed to an algorithm translating raw IMU data into quantifiable metrics for dystonic movement severity, distinguishing sustained/irregular dystonic patterns from rhythmic tremor.
  • Translated a clinical assessment gap into an engineering design problem through literature review and stakeholder engagement with clinical and engineering teams.
  • Led operation and data management of a markerless motion capture system (Theia3D) for a CIHR-funded Ankle-Foot Orthoses study in the PROPEL Lab, under Dr. Jan Andrysek, supporting biomechanical assessment of pediatric gait pathology.
  • Designed and executed a comparative validation study benchmarking Theia3D markerless motion capture against the GAITRite instrumented walkway, assessing accuracy and feasibility for clinical gait lab integration.
  • Won Best Research Presentation Award at the 20th Annual Anne & David Ward Summer Research Program — 26 students selected from 1,600+ applicants.
  • Designed structural components, tubing, and housings for a 6-DOF robotic arm regulating an automated ICU oxygen flowmeter, incorporating a precision belt-tensioning system for accurate actuation.
  • Integrated servo motors, sensors, and control electronics, programming coordinated multi-axis motion with proper load distribution, torque limits, and repeatable positioning.
  • Performed kinematic analysis, deflection simulations, and system validation to optimize stiffness, actuator performance, and fluid-flow reliability.
  • Managed technical validation data for mechanical assemblies, interpreting test results to identify failure modes and ensuring compliance under municipal standards and operational requirements.
  • Assisted with local inspections of backflow prevention system parts, reviewing mechanical check valves, measuring pressure differentials, and testing anti-siphon mechanisms.
  • Collaborated with inspectors, engineers, and operations staff to outline inspection reports, organize data validation criteria, and improve the validation workflow across the team.
  • Kukkiwon Certified 4th Degree Black Belt with over 12 years of training experience.
  • Developed strong leadership skills coaching students of all ages, fostering a supportive environment that promotes growth, discipline, and teamwork.
  • Managed gym operations including phone inquiries, email correspondence, and sales.
03 — Things I've built

Projects

Bacterial Growth Bioreactor

BUILDING NOW2026

Low-cost, modular bioreactor for reproducible outer membrane vesicle (OMV) production in engineered E. coli — currently on Iteration 4.

  • Designing a low-cost, modular bioreactor to give reproducible OMV production from engineered E. coli, addressing the limited environmental control of standard shake-flask cultures.
  • Iteration 1 mapped out every function a bioreactor might need — motor-driven impeller, sparger, air filtration, and ports for probes and reagents — before deciding what to keep.
  • Iteration 2 simplified to the essentials: an Erlenmeyer flask on a magnetic stir plate for agitation, an air pump for aeration, and a custom 3D-printed lid housing an Arduino and OD600 sensor.
  • Iteration 3 refined the lid's port dimensions and added a dedicated elevated mount for the motor once it proved larger than expected, while thinning the stand to reduce print material.
  • Currently building and testing Iteration 4.
Iteration 1 — concept sketch. Mapped every function a bioreactor might need before deciding what to keep: motor-driven impeller, sparger, air filtration, and ports for probes and reagents.

Ward Research Project — AFO Analysis

Aug 2026

Comparative clinical gait study on traditional vs. digitally fabricated ankle-foot orthoses in pediatric patients.

  • Designed and conducted a comparative clinical gait study evaluating traditional and digitally fabricated AFOs in pediatric participants with lower-limb impairments.
  • Applied quantitative gait analysis techniques using the GAITRite® system to collect and interpret walking speed, step-length symmetry, and single-support symmetry measures.
  • Contributed to an interdisciplinary pediatric rehabilitation research project, developing skills in clinical research, participant testing, data analysis, and translating findings into patient-centred orthotic care.
Research poster presented at the 20th Annual Anne & David Ward Summer Research Program.

Lower Limb Exoskeleton

May 2026

Wearable lower-limb exoskeleton with anatomically-modeled linkages custom-fit to individual pilot geometry.

  • Built for the ACE competition at McMaster University to perform firefighter-like tasks — climbing stairs, carrying weight, kicking down doors — with the suit using AI to predict the pilot's next move and assist through electrical actuation and mechanical load distribution.
  • Engineered a wearable lower-limb exoskeleton with anatomically-modeled linkages custom-fit to individual pilot geometry, integrating a motor control system to actuate joint movement and assist gait.
  • Modeled lower-limb linkages, joint mechanisms, and gearbox assemblies in SolidWorks, using anatomical imaging and musculoskeletal data to align linkage geometry and joint placement with individual pilot anatomy.
  • Performed kinematic and load-distribution analyses in Autodesk Inventor and SolidWorks to optimize gearbox design and torque transmission, enhancing joint stability and mechanical efficiency.

Automated Oxygen Flowmeter

Sept 2025

Precision oxygen flow regulation assembly for ICU delivery systems, validated against safety and manufacturability constraints.

  • Designed and optimized a precision oxygen flow regulation assembly incorporating electromechanical valves, pressure-rated fittings, and sealed interfaces to ensure accurate, leak-free oxygen delivery under variable inlet pressures.
  • Performed pressure–flow modeling, tolerance stack-up, and mechanical failure analysis to validate system robustness, prevent over-pressurization, and ensure compliance with ICU safety requirements.
  • Developed a modular, manufacturable mechanical architecture compatible with both wall-mounted and portable oxygen systems, emphasizing serviceability and medical-grade material selection.

JOYTAP — Assistive Stylus Tapper

Feb 2025

Responsive assistive device for manual dexterity impairment, built on a Raspberry Pi with closed-loop sensor control.

  • Engineered a responsive assistive device addressing manual dexterity impairment, integrating a Raspberry Pi, BNO055 sensor, and LKY62 servos, using sensor fusion and calibrated PWM cycles to optimize mechanical linkages for high-accuracy actuation.
  • Developed Python-based firmware using RPi.GPIO to implement real-time, closed-loop control, ensuring stable sensor-actuator coordination and reliable embedded system performance.
Final prototype of the functional JoyTap device.
